clue.text: Approves current demands

blocks.note: AC is alternating current
to demand something as yours is to claim it

explanation.surface: A regulator signs off on whatever the latest demands happen to be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as an adjective meaning present-day, but it is the electrical abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To acclaim is to praise loudly and publicly, a strong form of showing approval.

clue.text: Port and beer by Adrian Turner

indicators.note: someone who turns things over changes their order, so the letters get rearranged

blocks.note: ale is a kind of beer
the multiplication sign, as in 3 by 4
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Adrian Turner is offered port and beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner' looks like Adrian's surname, but it is the anagram signal. 'By' becomes X as in measurements like six by four.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandria is a major Egyptian seaport on the Mediterranean coast, founded by Alexander the Great.

clue.text: What goes with fish and chips in Epsom for Spooner?

definitions.text: What goes with fish and chips

indicators.note: Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version swaps initial sounds

blocks.note: Epsom racecourse is in the county of Surrey, so it is a Surrey course; swap the opening sounds

explanation.surface: A riddle about the right accompaniment for fish and chips at the Epsom races.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom is a racecourse in Surrey, home of the Derby. Said with a non-rhotic British accent, 'course' and 'sauce' rhyme, which makes the swap work.
explanation.definitionFit: Curry sauce poured over chips is a classic order at a British fish and chip shop.

clue.text: Gold-plated end is so long

indicators.note: plating coats an object all over, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to die is to come to an end

explanation.surface: A gilded finish on something takes so very long.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So long' reads as 'such a long time', but here it is the casual farewell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are ways of saying goodbye; the French farewell is used in English as a parting word.

clue.text: Countries following high speed intrigue

indicators.note: coming after something places it later in the line, setting the order of the two parts

blocks.note: Mach 1 is the speed of sound, with the 1 written as the letter I
nations are countries

explanation.surface: Nations race to keep up with some fast-moving international plotting.
explanation.walkthrough: Mach numbers measure speed relative to sound; MACH I reads as Mach one.
explanation.definitionFit: Machinations are scheming plots, and intrigue is the secret plotting they amount to.

clue.text: Bargain with Yorkshire Ripper, ultimately a killer

indicators.note: what comes ultimately comes at the very end, so only final letters are wanted

blocks.note: a snip is British slang for a bargain
the last letter of each word

explanation.surface: Someone strikes a deal with a notorious serial killer.
explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Ripper was a real murderer, which makes the surface feel grim, but he is only there for two end letters. In Britain a snip is something cheap.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniper shoots people from a hidden position at long range, so is a kind of killer.

clue.text: Cabaret near the centre of Luton found by driver?

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so just the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: nigh is an old word for near
the middle of five letters
a driver is a golf club; the question mark flags the example

explanation.surface: A cabaret venue in the middle of Luton, located by a taxi driver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' suggests a motorist, but it is the long-distance golf club. Luton is an English town north of London.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabaret is an evening venue with entertainment and drinks, much like a nightclub.

clue.text: If, say, Englishman kept his head …

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: Pom is Australian slang for an English person
the first letter of the Englishman's own name

explanation.surface: If, for instance, an Englishman kept calm under pressure, the clue trails off.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling's poem If opens 'If you can keep your head when all about you are losing theirs', which the surface echoes. The ellipsis links into the next clues.
explanation.definitionFit: If is a famous Rudyard Kipling poem, so it is one example of the wider category.

clue.text: … and in speech, regretted offensive …

indicators.note: in speech means spoken rather than written, so a word is matched by sound

blocks.note: to rue is to regret, and the past form sounds the same

explanation.surface: The speaker regretted saying something insulting, continuing from the previous clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses chain this to the clues before and after to make a running sentence that means nothing on its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Rude remarks are impolite and give offence, so offensive is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Half of headphones are broken with silence heard

indicators.note: something broken has its parts disordered, so the letters are rearranged
what is heard is taken by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
peace is quiet, and a homophone gives the other spelling

explanation.surface: One side of a pair of headphones has stopped working, leaving only silence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to describe a fault, but 'broken' works on the short word beside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones have two earpieces, one for each ear, so a single unit is half the set.

clue.text: Silver wind instrument is OK

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
a reed instrument such as the oboe is a wind instrument

explanation.surface: A silver flute or clarinet is acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind instrument' suggests a flute or trumpet; the setter wants the family name for oboes and clarinets.
explanation.definitionFit: Said as a reply, both words signal consent or assent to what someone has just proposed.

clue.text: … one in the Royal Navy might find nice workplace after right promotion

indicators.note: coming after places a piece at the end of the line
promotion moves someone up and out of their old place, so a letter leaves its spot

blocks.note: pretty means nice or attractive
an office is a place of work
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sailor could land a pleasant office job after a step up in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: The R in PRETTY OFFICE is lifted out and moved to the end, which is the 'promotion'. The ellipsis continues the chain from the previous clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A petty officer is a non-commissioned rank in the Royal Navy, roughly a sergeant equivalent.

clue.text: Play to suit solvers

blocks.note: first meaning: a Shakespeare comedy
second meaning: in whatever way pleases you, the people solving

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like a game made easy for solvers; the second half addresses the reader directly as 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a Shakespeare comedy and also a phrase meaning arranged according to your own preference.

clue.text: At first, Darwin and his theory got independent treatment

indicators.note: what comes at first is at the very front, so only an opening letter is kept

blocks.note: its opening letter
Darwin's famous theory of natural selection

explanation.surface: Darwin's theory was originally given a separate, independent hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His' points back to Darwin, so his theory is the one he is famous for.
explanation.definitionFit: Devolution hands powers from a central government to regions, giving them a measure of self-rule.

clue.text: Hero myth at variance with Philistine’s alternative role

indicators.note: being at variance means being at odds or out of line, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A heroic legend clashes with the setter's other persona.
explanation.walkthrough: Philistine is this puzzle's setter, so the definition is the setter speaking of himself. Wearing another hat means taking on another role.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing a different hat is an idiom for acting in another capacity, so the setter's alternative role is that hat.

clue.text: Medic in the morning facing a crisis

blocks.note: Dr is short for doctor
a.m. marks morning times
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor on the early shift confronts an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Facing' just joins the wordplay to the definition, like 'meeting'.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is an exciting, turbulent situation, which in everyday talk is close to a crisis.

clue.text: Squabbles are not about sticker beginning to stick

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps another
the beginning of a word is its opening, so just the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the contraction of these two words
gum is a sticky adhesive
its opening letter

explanation.surface: Rows break out that have nothing to do with a label starting to peel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Are not' collapses into its contraction, which then wraps around the sticky stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Squabbles are petty quarrels, and arguments are disputes between people who disagree.

clue.text: Big guns vessel internally in poor condition

indicators.note: something held internally is inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: an artery is a blood vessel
ill means unwell, in poor health

explanation.surface: A warship armed with heavy guns turns out to be in a bad state inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship carrying guns; it is a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Artillery means large-calibre guns such as cannons and howitzers, as opposed to small arms.

clue.text: Isn’t it commonly love that keeps gear hidden?

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the slangy spoken contraction of the two words
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a cog is a gear wheel

explanation.surface: A slangy question about whether love keeps one's equipment out of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innit' is informal British speech for 'isn't it', which 'commonly' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone incognito has their true identity concealed, so they are hidden in plain sight.

clue.text: Swell port?

blocks.note: surface reading: an excellent glass of port wine
setter's reading: the left side, L, placed inside a vessel, since port is a ship's left

explanation.walkthrough: 'Swell' poses as the old slang for excellent; it is the verb meaning to puff up. Port is the left side of a ship, so L sits in BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To bloat is to swell up or become distended, usually with gas or liquid.

clue.text: Muck about, you said, with reality in the making

indicators.note: to go about something is to surround it, so one piece wraps the others
what is said is spoken, so a word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: manure is dung, farmyard muck
the letter sounds like the pronoun
a fact is a reality

explanation.surface: Someone fools around while saying real things are being invented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muck about' looks like the phrase for messing around; split it and 'about' wraps the dung around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufacture as a noun is the making of goods, the process of producing things.

clue.text: Funny magazine

blocks.note: first meaning: amusing, causing laughter
second meaning: a periodical of strip cartoons

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it sounds like a humorous publication, which is close to right; the trick is that each word alone gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something amusing and a noun for a periodical made of illustrated cartoon stories.

clue.text: Discothèque welcomes Billy Connolly?

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them inside, so the word holds the answer within it

blocks.note: letters three to six of the word

explanation.surface: A nightclub lets in a famous comedian.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Connolly is a Glaswegian comedian, so the question mark marks him as one example of the category.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Connolly comes from Glasgow, making him a famous example of a person from Scotland.

clue.text: Prison disturbance

blocks.note: first meaning: slang for jail
second meaning: a commotion or fuss

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a prison riot, but the two words are separate meanings; 'in stir' is old British slang for being locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for a jail and also means a commotion that causes excitement or upset.

clue.text: Twisting truth, stand by copper in adversarial action

indicators.note: twisting distorts the shape of things, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer bends the truth and stands by a fellow copper in a court fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' invites a police officer, as British slang, but it is the metal's symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: Cut and thrust, from swordplay, is a lively exchange of attack and counter-attack, as in debate.

clue.text: Mischievous silence after seafood

indicators.note: coming after places a piece later in the line, fixing the order

blocks.note: scampi are breaded langoustines, a pub staple
the sound made to call for quiet

explanation.surface: A cheeky hush descends once the shellfish arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Scampi is a breaded shellfish dish common on British pub menus.
explanation.definitionFit: A scamp is a playful rascal, so behaving like one is roguish and naughty.

clue.text: See 24
District court in pursuit of wayward prince

indicators.note: someone wayward goes astray, so the letters stray from their order
chasing something means coming behind it, so that piece goes last

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
Ct is the abbreviation for court

explanation.surface: A court chases a disobedient royal through the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' looks like a royal court to go with the prince, but it is only its two-letter abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A precinct is an administrative area of a city, such as a police district in the US.
